notes:
Summary: Evaluation focused on Redwood Dedicated capacity guarantees and autoscaling behavior for a production financial assistant. Need predictable throughput for trading desk assistance + embeddings/rerank for search.

Timeline / recent activity:
- 2026-02-18 discovery call (ff_2026-02-18_8472): discussed workload shapes, model candidates (vicuna-13b/q4 -> Redwood suggested quantized variants), initial QPS targets.
- 2026-02-25 security sync: sent SOC2 evidence checklist (Drive deck), legal asked for explicit EU/US residency controls.
- 2026-03-05 live benchmark session (ff_2026-03-05_9011): ran 3 load patterns (steady, diurnal, burst). Perf deck + raw logs in Drive.
- 2026-03-09 SE workshop: drafted autoscale policy options and warm pool sizing.

Workload details and targets (customer-provided):
- Primary workload: chat assistant (session-based), avg request ~225 tokens, peak concurrent sessions ~400-600, expected burst up to 1200 qps-equivalent tokens in market-open minutes.
- Secondary: embeddings for similarity search (batch jobs overnight), reranking for low-latency queries.
- Latency SLO: p50 < 60ms, p95 target 120-180ms (for 512 token decode path). Higher-latency acceptable for background rerank/embeddings.
- Throughput expectations: baseline sustained 150 rps, peak burst 700+ rps; sizing goal: 8-32 GPUs reserved depending on seasonality.

Reserved GPU planning (initial ask):
- Proposal: start with 8 A100-class reserved GPUs in us-east, warm-pool 2 nodes, allow autoscale up to 24 GPUs for peak with 10m cooldown.
- Customer wants clear mapping: expected rps per GPU for their model mix (SE to provide perf matrix).

Autoscaling & capacity mgmt (detailed asks / notes):
- Scale-up triggers: queue length > 80 for 30s OR average CPU/GPU util > 78% for 45s. Needs a fast-path for extreme bursts (market open): pre-warm + transient burst capacity.
- Scale-down: scale only after 10m sustained low-util and queue < 20; avoid thrash during diurnal patterns.
- Warm pools: suggested warm pool = 2 nodes per region (hot standby) to reduce cold-start latency; ability to pre-warm model caches (KV cache primed) is critical.
- Queueing behavior: prefer priority queue (premium customers first), FIFO per priority. Soft queue limits with graceful degradation (trim generation length) and hard drop for abuse.
- Fallbacks/routing: require automated fallback to smaller/quantized model on saturation (maintain functional degraded mode). Audit trail required when fallback used.

SLA negotiation points (customer priorities):
- Throughput SLO: guaranteed baseline throughput for reserved pool (e.g., 8 GPUs -> 150 rps sustained) with credits if not met.
- Latency SLO: p95 targets tied to model variant; credits for repeated misses.
- Regional failover: ability to redirect traffic within 60s if region degraded.
- Maintenance windows: prefer scheduled maintenance windows outside US market hours; advanced notice 72h.
- Runbooks and playbooks required for capacity exhaustion incidents; contact escalation path (24/7 on-call for production incidents).

POC success criteria:
- Demonstrate p95 <= 180ms for chat under 2-hour sustained 400 concurrent sessions.
- Show autoscale ramp from 8->16 GPUs within 3 mins under a synthetic burst pattern.
- Warm pool reduces cold model latency by >= 60%.
- Confirm audit logs for fallback/reroute events and encryption at rest with KMS.

Open questions / blockers to resolution:
- Legal: final data residency wording for EU customers (affects architecture).
- Perf: need per-GPU perf matrix for 13B vs 7B models under their token distribution.
- Pricing: enterprise committed pricing vs burst overage terms.
- SLA credit formula: customer pushed for credits tied to per-minute throughput shortfalls.

Next steps (short):
- 2026-03-15: deliver perf matrix & proposed autoscale policy doc.
- 2026-03-20 -> 2026-04-03: 2-week Dedicated POC (6 GPUs) in us-east; load scripts and test cases to be provided by Veridian.
- Legal/security: exchange redline for residency clause by 2026-03-22.

- SE note: "Recommend quantized model as fallback + warm pool of 2 nodes to handle spikes."
